symbol_repair_2026_11_07.how: by hand, line by line from the Word file: the converter that made the deposit (it dropped the table of contents and leading tabs and collapsed runs of spaces) is not available, and the copy of the WA converter that maps symbols lays the text out differently, so regenerating would have changed more than the restored characters. wa41_hand_repair.py checks that each deposit line equals its Word paragraph converted without symbols (leading whitespace stripped) and replaces it with the same paragraph converted by wa41_docx2txt_sym.py, which maps them; both are kept outside the repository.
symbol_repair_2026_11_07.from: the same Word file, mrdoc_48735.docx in this source bundle
symbol_repair_2026_11_07.why: the converter read only the text runs of word/document.xml and dropped every Word <w:sym> character. This file sets 25 that way, all in the Schedule 1 forms: 9 Wingdings ticks (F0FC) each followed by a Wingdings box (F072), and 7 Wingdings 2 boxes (F0A3).
symbol_repair_2026_11_07.what_changed: 25 characters, nothing else; no line added or removed. Lines 278-280, 282-284 and 291 (Part D, registration and fees, and Part E, approved breeder) and 329 and 331 (Part H, local government use): '():' is now '(✓): [ ]', the tick and the box to be ticked. Lines 424, 425, 428 and 431 (the things the warrant authorises seizing) and 436, 438 and 440 (the justice's grounds): each now begins '[ ]' and a tab, the box to be ticked.
symbol_repair_2026_11_07.checked: the diff against the previous deposit is the 16 lines above, and undoing the restored characters gives the previous deposit byte for byte
